name: Sparse table idempotent range query
definition: For x_1,…,x_n, S_{0,i}=x_i; S_{j,i}=S_{j−1,i}⊗S_{j−1,i+2^{j−1}} for 1≤i≤n−2^j+1 and j≥1. For 1≤a≤b≤n set j=⌊log₂(b−a+1)⌋ and Q(a,b)=S_{j,a}⊗S_{j,b−2^j+1}.
variables: n positive length; i one-based start; j nonnegative level; ⊗ closed associative idempotent operation; a,b inclusive endpoints
assumptions: Static nonempty array; exact associative and idempotent operation (u⊗u=u for every value in its closed domain); preserve operand order; integer index arithmetic
limitations: O(n log(n+1)) aggregate slots and preprocessing combines; two table reads and one combine per nonempty query with constant-time integer logarithm or precomputed lengths. No empty interval identity required; changes invalidate stored aggregates. Time bounds assume constant-cost combines and indexing
failure_conditions: Reject invalid or empty ranges and inconsistent table dimensions
Reject nonassociative or nonidempotent operations for overlapping lookup; reject stale table after input changes
computation: Fill singleton level, then each higher level using adjacent half-blocks at every valid start, including n−2^j+1. For a query obtain j by exact integer arithmetic or lookup, and combine left block then right block. Rebuild after data changes.

source.citation: Jeff Erickson (2025), Advanced Data Structures, Lecture 1: Range-Minimum Queries, section 1.1 Sparse Lookup Table, pp. 1–2 and footnote 2. https://jeffe.cs.illinois.edu/teaching/datastructures/notes/01-RMQ-LCA.pdf

application: General static nonempty range aggregation; no empirical benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Immutable indexed array and associative idempotent operation.
incompatible_methods: Using overlapping blocks for ordinary sums or other nonidempotent operations
mechanism_note: The two blocks cover the interval with contiguous overlap; the ordered product has form A⊗B⊗B⊗C, omitting empty outside pieces, and reduces to A⊗B⊗C by associativity and idempotence. Commutativity is not needed. The source treats minimum; this generalized ordered formulation is independently derived. Corrects the printed build loop upper endpoint to n−L+1. Distinct static overlapping-block lookup rather than disjoint mutable segment-tree traversal.

name: Disjoint set union with rank and path compression
definition: For 1≤i≤n initialize parent_i=i and rank_i=0. Find(i)=i if parent_i=i, otherwise parent_i←Find(parent_i), returning that root. For u=Find(a), v=Find(b), if u=v do nothing; otherwise exchange u,v if rank_u<rank_v, set parent_v←u, and if rank_u=rank_v set rank_u←rank_u+1.
variables: n positive universe size; a,b,i valid item indices; parent_i parent pointer; rank_i nonnegative historical height bound; u,v representative roots
assumptions: Fixed finite universe of singleton sets; sequential operations; all indices valid; only merging and membership queries; deterministic tie rule chooses first root after rank ordering
limitations: O(n) space; O(log(n+1)) worst-case pointer traversal per find or union and O(m(1+α(n))) total amortized time for m operations including n singleton creations under standard union-find analysis. α is an inverse Ackermann function; not a constant worst-case guarantee. Compression does not support arbitrary splitting or deletion; representatives can change after union
failure_conditions: Reject invalid indices or inconsistent parent pointers, cycles other than root self-links, or violated rank invariants
Do not apply sequential update rules concurrently without a separately justified synchronization design
computation: Initialize singleton roots. Traverse parent links to find the representative and redirect every visited nonroot to that representative. Merge only distinct roots, placing lower rank below higher rank and incrementing only the surviving rank on a tie. Keep nonroot ranks unchanged.

source.citation: Stajano and Sauerwald (2015), University of Cambridge Algorithms, 5.3 Disjoint Sets, slides 9–11; Tarjan (1975), Efficiency of a Good But Not Linear Set Union Algorithm, JACM 22(2), 215–225, DOI 10.1145/321879.321884 (bibliographic metadata and abstract checked). https://www.cl.cam.ac.uk/teaching/1415/Algorithms/disjointsets.pdf

application: General incremental maintenance of equivalence classes; no empirical benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Fixed universe and sequence of valid union and representative queries.
incompatible_methods: Using rank as exact current height after path compression
Incrementing rank on an already-connected union
mechanism_note: Each parent edge strictly increases rank, excluding nonroot cycles. A root of rank r represents at least 2^r elements by induction on equal-rank mergers; compression changes no membership. The resulting logarithmic depth bound is independent of the cited stronger amortized theorem. This maintains arbitrary partitions, whereas Kruskal uses connectivity as a subroutine in a weighted graph algorithm.
